title: Apricot Frangipane Tart with Brown Sugar
changes_from_base: Fresh apricot halves on a rich brown sugar frangipane baked slowly in an unbaked case, in place of poached pears.
summary: Ripe apricot halves sunk into a deep, caramel-like brown sugar frangipane and baked low and slow.
equipment: 23 cm loose-based tart tin, 3 cm deep

ingredients.item: plain flour, plus extra for rolling
fine sea salt or table salt
light brown sugar, plus 25 g for sprinkling
small ripe but firm apricots, halved and stoned

steps.title: Pastry
steps.text: pulse the butter, flour and salt to fine crumbs. Add the icing sugar, yolk and water and pulse just until it gathers. Knead lightly until smooth, wrap and chill 30 min.

steps.title: Frangipane
steps.text: grind the almonds finely and tip into the bowl. Process the 200 g brown sugar, butter and vanilla until fluffy, then with the motor running add the flour and eggs. Pulse in the ground almonds.

steps.title: Line
steps.text: roll the pastry about 5 mm thick on a floured surface, press it into the tin and trim. Chill 1 h.

steps.title: Assemble
steps.text: heat the oven to 165 °C (145 °C fan) with the tray on the middle shelf. Spread the frangipane in the raw case and nestle in the apricot halves, cut side up. Sprinkle the remaining sugar into the hollows. The frangipane goes into an unbaked case; the long bake cooks both.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: set the tin on the hot tray and bake about 1 h 15 min, until golden and set. Cover loosely with foil if the top browns too quickly.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: trim any overflow, loosen the sides and cool completely in the tin. Serve with crème fraîche. It slices cleanly only once fully cool.

tips: Choose apricots that are ripe but firm so they hold their shape.
The frangipane can be made a day ahead; bring it to room temperature first.
Plums or peach halves work in the same way.
safety: Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep covered at room temperature for 2 days, or in the fridge for 4 days.
